hints: Focus on how many bonding pairs and lone pairs surround the central phosphorus atom in $\text{PF}_5$.
Phosphorus forms five P-F bonds using all five of its valence electrons, so count what is left over for a lone pair.
Recall the shape for five bonding pairs with no lone pairs, then check its bond angles and symmetry to test each statement.
walkthrough:
**Count the electron pairs around phosphorus**

Phosphorus is in Group 15, so it has 5 valence electrons. In $\text{PF}_5$ it forms 5 single bonds to fluorine.

That means 5 bonding pairs and 0 lone pairs:
$$5 \text{ bonding pairs} + 0 \text{ lone pairs} = 5 \text{ electron pairs}$$

**Predict the shape**

Five bonding pairs with no lone pairs repel to get as far apart as possible. This gives a trigonal bipyramidal shape.

Think of a triangle around the middle with one F above and one F below the phosphorus.

**Check angles, polarity and name**

A trigonal bipyramid does not have all angles the same. It has $90^{\circ}$, $120^{\circ}$ and $180^{\circ}$ F-P-F angles.

It is also highly symmetrical, so the five P-F bond dipoles cancel and there is no overall dipole. It is not octahedral, which needs 6 bonds.

options.A: Incorrect. In trigonal bipyramidal $\text{PF}_5$ there are three different F-P-F angles: $90^{\circ}$ between axial and equatorial, $120^{\circ}$ between equatorial positions, and $180^{\circ}$ between the two axial positions. So not every angle is $90^{\circ}$.
options.B: Correct. Phosphorus uses all 5 valence electrons to make 5 P-F bonding pairs. There are no electrons left on P for a lone pair, which is why $\text{PF}_5$ is an example of an expanded octet with 10 electrons around P.
options.C: Incorrect. Although each P-F bond is polar, the trigonal bipyramidal shape is symmetrical. The bond dipoles cancel vectorially, so $\text{PF}_5$ is non-polar with zero overall dipole moment.
options.D: Incorrect. Octahedral is the shape for 6 bonding pairs and no lone pairs, for example $\text{SF}_6$. With 5 bonding pairs and no lone pairs, $\text{PF}_5$ is trigonal bipyramidal.
